title: Euclid telescope spots oldest quasars ever discovered, adding to "perplexing" space mystery
facts: An international team of astronomers discovered 31 ancient quasars using the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope. [cite: 252]
The Euclid space telescope operates at a stable hovering position approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. [cite: 252]
The group of 31 newly discovered quasars includes the two oldest quasars ever observed. [cite: 252]
Light from the two oldest discovered quasars originated when the universe was approximately 670 million years old. [cite: 252]
The current estimated age of the universe is 13.8 billion years. [cite: 252]
The recent Euclid telescope discovery beats the previous 2021 record for the oldest known quasar by approximately 20 million years. [cite: 252]
The European Space Agency launched the Euclid space telescope in 2023. [cite: 252]
The Euclid telescope doubled the number of ancient quasars known to science within two years of operation. [cite: 252]
Daming Yang is the lead author of the Euclid quasar study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. [cite: 252]
The newly discovered quasars date back to the epoch of reionization in cosmic history. [cite: 252]
The James Webb space telescope also conducted recent observations of the newly announced ancient quasars. [cite: 252]
The Euclid telescope captured a highly detailed image containing 60 million stars at the center of the Milky Way galaxy. [cite: 252]
The Euclid telescope captured an image of the Abell 2390 galaxy cluster encompassing more than 50,000 galaxies in 2024. [cite: 252]
The Abell 2390 galaxy cluster is located 2.7 billion light years away from Earth. [cite: 252]
The Euclid space telescope was launched from Cape Canaveral atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. [cite: 252]
